newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Salomon downgrades Irkutskenergo to hold.
newsitem.headline: Salomon downgrades Irkutskenergo to hold.

text.p: Salomon Brothers is downgrading Russian regional utility Irkutskenergo to hold because the share price already reflects the company's short-term prospects, the U.S. investment bank said in a research note.
The note, dated February 7, said Irkutskenergo 1996 results will be unimpressive: the forecast 39 percent growth in revenues will translate into a 61 percent fall in profits in dollar terms.

Collection of electricity bills will fall by three percent against 1995 levels, while cash collection will remain at 1995 levels of 24 percent of total collection, the note, by analyst Alexander Kazbegi said.
Salomon Brothers forecast consumption of Irkutskenergo electricity would fall by eight percent, while heat consumption will rise by two percent.
A growth in tariffs will help dollar revenues rise by 17 percent in 1997, Salomon Brothers said.
"We expect high costs and taxes in 1997 and 1998 to depress quick recovery of net earnings," it said.
Irkutskenergo fell to $0.269 on Thursday on the Russian Trading System from $0.288 at Wednesday's close.
